summary.text: Robert C. Carroll is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent in Assembly District 44, which covers Park Slope, Kensington, and Prospect Heights in Brooklyn. A Brooklyn native and former election lawyer, he was first elected to the Assembly in 2016 and chairs its Libraries and Education Technology Committee. His official biography highlights his work on dyslexia and literacy, renewable energy, election law, and public transportation, and he advanced from his 2026 primaries without appearing on the ballot.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in the 44th Assembly District; attended PS 230 in Kensington. He struggled with dyslexia as a child, which he says shaped his legislative focus on literacy.
Graduate of SUNY Binghamton and holds a J.D. from New York Law School. His official biography describes him as a former election lawyer.

Before running for the Assembly, he was an attorney and served as president of the Central Brooklyn Independent Democrats, a political club serving Park Slope and Windsor Terrace; a 2016 report said he was the club's youngest president. In 2016 he described himself as a reformer.

Elected to the Assembly in 2016 to succeed Jim Brennan, who did not seek re-election; Carroll won the 2016 Democratic primary with about 90% of the vote and the general election with about 85%, also running on the Working Families Party line.

Chairs the Assembly Committee on Libraries and Education Technology and serves on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Election Law; Environmental Conservation; and Tourism, Parks, Arts and Sports Development Committees.

Has authored and passed 35 bills through the Legislature since being elected, 25 of which have been signed into law. His official biography names his work on environmental legislation, early childhood literacy, election law reform, and public transportation.

Prime sponsor of the Build Public Renewables Act, included in the 2023-24 state budget, and author of the Dyslexia Task Force Act and the Dyslexia Diagnosis Access Act (signed 2024), according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he lives in Park Slope with his wife Virginia and their two children.
